page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon processors, which correspond to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The instance is configured with 360.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory allocation of 3.75 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. The n1-standard-96 exhibits weak single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance is strong, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 3918.64 GB/sec and uncached large-block read speeds at 213.36 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%.

Given its high resource density and strong multi-core scaling, this instance is suitable for highly parallelized workloads such as multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and moderate database operations. However, its weak single-threaded performance and poor text generation speeds in LLM inference make it less optimal for single-core bound tasks or real-time generative AI. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-96 offers a high volume of legacy Intel Xeon vCPUs and memory bandwidth, making it a viable option for parallel processing tasks that do not require modern instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX.
